text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THAWRA
- Iraq asks Turkey to withdraw its troops from the northern parts of the country.
- Iraq's justice minister says in Ankara that Turkey's security problems will end once Baghdad extends its authority once again over northern Iraq.
- An Arab parliamentary meeting in Cairo calls for an end to the sanctions on Iraq and Libya.
- Britain says it respects Iraq's territorial integrity.
- Russia imposes its conditions on NATO.
- OPEC expects oil prices to rise again.
- Sudan pardons political prisoners.
- Izzat Ibrahim, vice-chairman of the Revolutionary Command Council, holds meeting on how to implement this year's harvest plans.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz receives Brazilian official.
- U.N. resolutions do not bar flights by Iraqi civilian planes.
- Two ships loaded with cooking oil anchor at Umm Qasr port in southern Iraq.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and QADISSIYA)
- Commentary says U.S. attempts to harm Iraq are futile.
- Article on the notion of justice in President Saddam Hussein's writings.
- Article on how to improve national industries.
QADISSIYA
- Editorial lashes out at the United States for anti-Iraq stands.
- Article on role of incentives in boosting production.
